runbooks.diagnosis: calendar-radicale deliberately shares the calendar container's netns (network_mode: "service:calendar", pinned static IP on opensme-net; traefik labels moved to calendar). 'docker compose up --wait calendar' recreates the netns owner but NOT the passenger — radicale keeps running in the orphaned old netns (loopback only) — so calrs sync to http://calendar-radicale:5232/ fails with 'tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)' and the edge /dav route 502s, while the compose command itself exits 0.
remediation: docker compose up -d --wait calendar calendar-radicale (bring owner AND passenger up together)
Verify a calendar sync lands (Last Synced updates) and /u/demo/vc returns 200
Keep the calendar-setup step that brings up the pair as one step

runbooks.diagnosis: Radicale serializes a collection's resourcetype with an uppercase prefix and a space (<C:calendar />), so scripts that grep for '<c:calendar/>' never match — they fall through and issue MKCALENDAR on an existing collection, getting a benign 409. A calrs sync that relies on the probe can report 'zero calendars'.
remediation: Probe for the spaced/uppercase form <C:calendar /> or use PROPFIND 207 and check the tag presence
Treat MKCALENDAR 409 on an existing collection as a warn, not an error

runbooks.diagnosis: SOGo's ICS/CalDAV fetcher is https-only and rejects private IPs, so the booking store is exposed read-only at the edge on calendar.<host>/dav/ with Radicale htpasswd on top of the edge route (RADICALE_USER/RADICALE_PASSWORD) — the internal http address must never be handed to SOGo's subscription.
remediation: Keep the edge /dav route with basic-auth (radicale htpasswd) for SOGo subscriptions and calrs
Never point a SOGo subscription at an internal http:// IP
When adding/removing edge auth, update calrs and SOGo together — they share the route
